scope: Six source-informed extractor questions and four coordinator wordings across the three episodes. Existing source/answers seen; not blind. Frozen before first retrieval and become development cases after use.

cases.question: Why did Cam recognize Kat as Canadian, and did that mean her NES boxes were PAL?
cases.expected: Her French/English box text tipped him off; the hosts distinguish Canadian bilingual/Mattel packaging from automatic PAL identification. Cam says he has no boxed NES games, and Johnny's Canadian black-box subset is only a future low-priority wish.

cases.question: Which manufacturer did Johnny accidentally attach to the CD-i, and how was he corrected?
cases.expected: He says Panasonic and is corrected to Philips, rendered Phillips in the transcript. Preserve this as an in-episode correction, not confirmation that the hosts performed a catalog audit or that all games on either criticized system are worthless.

cases.question: Does Johnny's ninety-hour Dragon Warrior VII save tell us how long he actively played?
cases.expected: No. He gives an approximate save-file figure and explains he sometimes fell asleep with the game running during illness. It is not a completion time, benchmark, diagnosis or verified account of illness causation.

cases.question: Can we tell from this episode who owned Blazing Lazers on Wii Virtual Console?
cases.expected: The Wii ownership remark is unlabelled and should remain actor-uncertain. Cam is clearly the speaker reporting first completion on Thursday, but that does not automatically assign the separate Wii copy to him. No audio verification was performed.

cases.question: What was Johnny's workaround for Canadian import costs, and did Cam really book an expo trip?
cases.expected: Johnny proposes saving avoided fees toward a Portland trip and wants an Instagram meetup. Cam's supposed commitment emerges in teasing banter; no booking or attendance is reported. Customs and price statements are historical host claims, not present travel/tax advice.

cases.question: What would Johnny's ideal big-screen handheld setup look like, and what limits did he acknowledge?
cases.expected: He praises GameCube with Game Boy Player and a SNES-style Hori controller, and wishes for a Wii U DS player using its two screens. He acknowledges touch-heavy DS games would not all fit the idea, and EarthBound is an RPG-library exception. This is preference and a hypothetical accessory, not proof of an announced product, universal compatibility or legal approval.

cases.question: Was Tyler's Portland game already on its way to him?
cases.expected: No; Johnny still had the boxed purchase and needed to go to the post office. No shipment or delivery established; title caption uncertain.

cases.question: Was the Stadium Events on Johnny's shelf the same authentic collectible Stephan received?
cases.expected: No; guest received authentic North American copy as wife-funded gift, whereas Johnny identifies a reproduction. No current family or ownership inference beyond source.

cases.question: What did the outro correct about Animal Crossing card packs?
cases.expected: Original retail price corrected to2.99; earlier higher remembered amounts associated with resale, not a present price or a standard game pack-in.

cases.question: Did Tyler keep his little GameCube gum cases or replace them?
cases.expected: Threw them away in a memorabilia purge, later regrets it and wants them back but refuses imagined high replacement price. No replacement purchased.
